title: RBZ Jewellers Ltd - 544060 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: RBZ Jewellers Q4 FY26 revenue rose 38% YoY to INR190 crore and FY26 PAT rose 41% to INR55 crore; management gave no FY27 guidance.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR190 crore (+38% YoY), with EBITDA of INR21 crore (+46%, margin 11.19%, +63 bps) and PAT of INR12 crore (+36%). For FY26, revenue was INR637 crore (+20%), EBITDA INR92 crore (+43%, margin 14.44%, +233 bps) and PAT INR55 crore (+41%, margin 8.61%). Growth was supported by Akshay Tritiya and an early Akshay Tritiya (19 April 2026) pulled sales into late March. Management declined to give FY27 guidance, citing the recent government gold-import and customs duty announcements and the Prime Minister's request to defer gold purchases, and said it would reassess by around August.

financial_highlights.value: INR1,251 crore (retail INR408 crore; B2B INR843 crore)
INR56 crore at March 2026 (vs INR17 crore, as cited by analyst)
financial_highlights.change: Spike from late-March sales; management says now normalised

segments.name: Retail (B2C, Ahmedabad flagship)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR121 crore, +31% YoY. Management cites roughly 35% daily wear and 65% occasion wear mix in retail; FY26 retail merchandise value INR408 crore.

segments.name: Wholesale (B2B)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR67 crore, +57% YoY. Management said wholesale rose to 56% of B2B mix in Q4 as some job work customers shifted to wholesale. Indicative GP 7-8%.

segments.name: Job work
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue approx. INR1 crore. Management says corporate jewellers shifted toward job work due to gold price increases, but volumes fell as gold price doubled. Indicative GP 6-8% for B2B.

guidance_outlook: No FY27 revenue or profit guidance; management said it would reserve guidance and reassess after April/May trends and the market reaction, with a fuller view possibly by around August 2026 (IIJS).

Surat and Rajkot large-format stores targeted to commence operations by Q2 FY27; two more stores (Gandhinagar and Maninagar, mid-format) targeted within calendar 2026, with the season timing as the target.
Debt target about 1:1 to 1.2:1 at peak for the four new stores in FY27, with a 1.4-1.5x leverage ceiling; management said FY27 equity of about INR300 crore is expected.
Management said it is not planning manufacturing capex at present, as capacity utilisation is about 50-55%.
Inventory of INR125-150 crore required per large-format store; management says no equity dilution is needed and debt, inventory transfer and profit will fund it.
capex_capacity: Capacity utilisation is about 50-55% per management, which is well below peak; no manufacturing capex planned for now.

Management says rupee capacity has risen to about INR3,000 crore from about INR1,200 crore at IPO, because gold prices rose from about INR60,000 to INR1.5 lakh per 10 grams, while artisan output is still about 1,000 grams per month.
Four stores planned in calendar 2026: Surat and Rajkot (large format, Q2 FY27) and Gandhinagar and Maninagar (mid-format, timing 'within the calendar year').
Daily wear in-house production planned to start from Q1 FY27 with dedicated infrastructure; B2B daily wear pilot at IIJS.
Carat mix: 18-carat antique and some colour-stone collections being sold to corporates; low-carat antique still at an experimental stage.
demand_pricing: Management said April 2026 was very good; May was not yet complete at the call date.
Gold price rise has shifted corporate demand from wholesale to job work, but job work volumes fell as value per gram rose. Management expects both B2B streams combined to matter.
Consumer exchange share is about 40-50% of jewellery, with new buying at 50-60%, according to management. Exchange activity has risen somewhat, per management.
Government announcement on gold import duty and advance authorisation, plus the PM's request to defer gold purchases: management expects limited impact in the low season but is watching for a dent.

Competition: Shringar entering plain-gold wedding jewellery; management sees no direct overlap with its antique segment. Gujarat described as a white space with little chain presence of pan-India players.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of recent customs duty hike and advance authorisation changes on gold imports on volumes, revenue and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is too early and it is watching ground-level reaction over a week or two. It expects limited impact in the post-Akshay Tritiya low season and no comment until there is something concrete.

qa_highlights.question: Will gold metal loan (GML) usage rise, and how is gold hedged?
qa_highlights.answer: Management plans to explore GML for buying gold for new stores. Inventory is kept about 20-25% below market price, and it will hedge forward once prices reach parity.

qa_highlights.question: Inventory gains in FY26 and profit excluding gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated inventory gains of INR10-12 crore and said PAT without gold price gains would be roughly INR40-45 crore. It added that GML would have halved interest cost, to roughly INR8 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did trade receivables rise from INR17 crore to INR56 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to late-March sales around the IIJS Bangalore exhibition and an early Akshay Tritiya, with receivables now back to normal. Wholesale debtor days are about 30.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 guidance and expansion outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no FY27 guidance, saying it would wait for April/May trends and market reaction, and expects to reassess by around August. It is confident about the long-term store expansion.

qa_highlights.question: Mix of studded and lab-grown diamond jewellery?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not doing lab-grown diamonds and is focused on antique gold. It sees potential in studded/diamond jewellery but it is not a current priority.

risks_watch: Government gold import duty and advance authorisation changes, and the PM's request to defer gold purchases, could hit demand and the wedding-season buying pattern.

Inventory: the store expansion needs roughly INR125-150 crore inventory per large store, raising peak debt to about 1:1.2 and increasing dependence on GML and short-term borrowing (INR120 crore short-term debt cited).
Receivables: trade receivables rose sharply to INR56 crore at March 2026; management has not disclosed the current balance.
Job work volumes fell as gold prices rose, and management said a shift to job work versus wholesale affects margin mix; FY27 job work outlook is not quantified.
Execution: Surat and Rajkot by Q2 FY27 and two mid-format stores in calendar 2026; the company has no guidance on their sales ramp-up.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the long-term store expansion and the Gujarat white-space thesis, but deliberately cautious on near-term numbers. Management declined FY27 guidance and deferred answers on the recent gold duty changes and the PM's request, saying it would wait for ground data.
key_quotes: The growth momentum was supported by festive demand, particularly during Akshay Tritiya season.
I think we are in a very comfortable situation with respect to debt equity ratios, etcetera.
There is no guidance for this year, frankly saying.
The best part about our company is, we are in occasion jewellery more. Hence, all the demand is linked through weddings.

growth.why: Management gave no FY27 revenue or profit guidance, citing gold import duty changes and the PM's request to defer gold purchases, and will reassess around August; store openings (Surat and Rajkot by Q2 FY27, Gandhinagar and Maninagar within calendar 2026) are the only concrete growth items, with utilisation at about 50-55% and no manufacturing capex.
